starterQuestions.q: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous carriers (Aa x Aa), what are the expected genotypic and phenotypic ratios?
starterQuestions.a: Genotypic ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa (1:2:1); phenotypic ratio is 3 dominant : 1 recessive (3:1).

starterQuestions.q: What geometric shapes represent males and females in standard clinical pedigree charts?
starterQuestions.a: Squares represent males; circles represent females.

starterQuestions.q: What pedigree observation definitively disproves an X-linked recessive mode of inheritance?
starterQuestions.a: Father-to-son (male-to-male) transmission of the trait (fathers pass only their Y chromosome to sons).

starterQuestions.q: Why is a testcross performed with a homozygous recessive individual (aa)?
starterQuestions.a: To determine whether an individual showing the dominant phenotype is homozygous dominant (AA) or heterozygous (Aa).

starterQuestions.q: What is the probability that a healthy, unaffected sibling of a child with an autosomal recessive condition is a carrier?
starterQuestions.a: 2 in 3 (2/3 or ~66.7%), because the homozygous recessive genotype (aa) is excluded from the surviving outcomes.

starterQuestions.q: State the mathematical rule used to calculate the joint probability of two independent genetic events occurring together.
starterQuestions.a: The Product Rule (multiplication rule: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)).

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: Monohybrid Crosses (Punnett Squares), Pedigree Chart Analysis & Inheritance Risk Calculations
deliverable: Construct and solve monohybrid crosses using 2x2 Punnett squares, interpret clinical pedigree charts across multiple generations to deduce inheritance modes (autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked recessive), and calculate conditional inheritance risk probabilities using the product and sum rules.

objectives.knowledge: Construct 2x2 Punnett squares for monohybrid crosses and identify standard clinical pedigree chart symbols.
objectives.application: Decode multi-generational pedigrees to deduce autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, and X-linked recessive inheritance modes.
objectives.evaluation: Combine monohybrid Punnett square probabilities with conditional pedigree analysis to calculate precise disease transmission and carrier risk probabilities.

terminology.def: A genetic mating analyzing the inheritance of a single gene locus with two alleles (yielding 3:1 phenotypic ratio for Aa x Aa).
A 2x2 grid representing the meiotic segregation of parental alleles into gametes and all possible fertilization genotypes.
Standardized genealogical symbols: squares (males), circles (females), Roman numerals (generations), and Arabic numbers (individuals).
The probability that an unaffected sibling of an autosomal recessive patient is a carrier: 2/3 (sample space restricted to AA and Aa).
Mating an individual with dominant phenotype to a homozygous recessive mate (aa) to deduce their genotype (1:1 ratio if heterozygous).

theoryPoints: Monohybrid Segregation: Mendel's First Law ensures each gamete carries only one allele per gene locus, producing equal proportions of dominant and recessive gametes in heterozygotes.
Pedigree Diagnostics: Look first for generational skipping (recessive) vs vertical continuity (dominant), and check sex ratios and father-son transmission (autosomal vs X-linked).

Obligate Carrier Identification: In autosomal recessive pedigrees, both parents of an affected child must be carriers (Aa). In X-linked recessive, all daughters of an affected father must be carriers (XAXa).
The 2/3 Sibling Rule: Phenotypically normal offspring of Aa x Aa crosses have genotypes 1 AA : 2 Aa, so carrier probability is 2/3.
Compound Risk Product Rule: P(affected child) = P(Mother is carrier) x P(Father is carrier) x P(both transmit recessive allele = 1/4).

workedExample.title: Monohybrid Cross & Pedigree Risk Calculation
workedExample.subtitle: Combining a 2x2 Punnett square with a 3-generation clinical pedigree tree for Cystic Fibrosis

steps.label: Step 1: Constructing the Monohybrid Punnett Square
steps.detail: Parental carrier cross: Aa x Aa. Gametes: A and a from each parent. 2x2 Punnett square yields genotypes: 1 AA (healthy non-carrier), 2 Aa (healthy carrier), 1 aa (affected CF). Phenotypic ratio: 3 healthy : 1 affected.

steps.label: Step 2: Deducing Sarah's Conditional Carrier Probability
steps.detail: Pedigree shows Sarah is the unaffected sister of an affected brother (aa). Since Sarah is healthy, the aa genotype is ruled out. Her genotype must be AA (1/3) or Aa (2/3). Sarah's carrier risk is 2/3.

steps.label: Step 3: Determining Partner's Population Carrier Probability
steps.detail: Her partner David has no family history of CF. In the UK population, the carrier frequency for CF is approximately 1 in 25 (1/25).

steps.label: Step 4: Applying the Product Rule for Total Offspring Risk
steps.detail: Risk of child having CF = P(Sarah is carrier = 2/3) x P(David is carrier = 1/25) x P(both transmit 'a' = 1/4) = 2/300 = 1/150 (~0.67%).

hingeQuestions.question: In a pedigree, two unaffected parents have a son and a daughter with a rare metabolic disorder. What is the definitive mode of inheritance?
hingeQuestions.explanation: Unaffected parents having affected children indicates recessive inheritance; both a male and female offspring are affected, confirming autosomal rather than X-linked or Y-linked.

hingeQuestions.question: A healthy man's brother died of Cystic Fibrosis. He marries a woman whose carrier status is unknown (general population carrier risk = 1/25). What is the probability that their first child will have Cystic Fibrosis?
hingeQuestions.explanation: Risk = P(Man is carrier = 2/3) x P(Woman is carrier = 1/25) x P(Both transmit mutant allele = 1/4) = 2/300 = 1/150.

hingeQuestions.question: A father affected with X-linked hypophosphataemic rickets (dominant) has children with an unaffected mother. What proportion of their children will inherit the condition?
options: Zero children (condition requires two mutant alleles)
hingeQuestions.explanation: An affected father passes his single affected X chromosome to 100% of his daughters, who will be affected because the trait is dominant. He passes his normal Y chromosome to all sons.

examQuestion.question: Analyze the inheritance pattern of an autosomal recessive condition in a three-generation pedigree, explain why unaffected siblings of affected individuals have a 2/3 carrier risk rather than 1/2, and calculate the overall risk of an affected child if an unaffected sibling marries an unrelated partner from a population where carrier frequency is 1 in 30. [6 marks]
guidance: Pedigree Diagnostic Criteria: Autosomal recessive disorders skip generations (horizontal pattern); unaffected parents of affected offspring are obligate carriers (Aa); equal sex incidence [2 marks].

Conditional 2/3 Carrier Probability: In an Aa x Aa cross, expected offspring genotypes are 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. Because an unaffected sibling cannot be 'aa', the denominator is restricted to 3 outcomes (1 AA and 2 Aa); therefore, 2 out of 3 possible genotypes are carriers (2/3 probability) [2 marks].
Risk Calculation: Apply the product rule: P(affected child) = P(sibling is carrier = 2/3) x P(partner is carrier = 1/30) x P(both transmit 'a' = 1/4) = 2/360 = 1/180 (~0.56%) [2 marks].

plenary: Pedigree charts provide a visual blueprint of genetic transmission across generations.
Recognize key diagnostic flags: generation skipping (recessive), vertical continuity (dominant), and male bias / lack of father-to-son transmission (X-linked).
Master conditional probability: unaffected siblings of autosomal recessive individuals are 2/3 carriers.
Next Lesson: Genetic disorders: Chromosomal abnormalities — nondisjunction mechanisms and karyotyping of aneuploidies.
